annotations.text:
Ending-soon warning, as built

The blocking dialog is gone. The warning is a notice that hangs under the status rail for 12 seconds, dismissible, and interrupts nothing: no scrim, no acknowledgement, no stopping whoever is speaking.

What makes the auto-dismiss safe is the chip. The countdown has been in the rail since the signal arrived and stays for the whole window, so the notice only has to be seen once.

The copy says what will happen, not what it feels like: "This meeting will end in about 9 minutes", from the existing ENDING_SOON_ONE_MINUTE / ENDING_SOON_MANY_MINUTES keys in all ten languages. The minute count is frozen when the warning lands rather than derived from the live timer, so it cannot tick down mid-sentence.

Real tokens, so both themes come for free: surface, border, text-primary, text-secondary, warn and hover from the meeting theme, 5px surface radius, Roboto.

Measured in a browser, not estimated

Desktop 360x70 at (16, 52). Phone 374x70 at (8, 44), edge to edge with 8px insets once the rail drops to 44px. At 320px wide it grows to 89px on three lines and still does not overflow. Landscape 844x390 checked too.

The close button is 40x40 at every width, matching the toolbar's own buttons. No horizontal overflow anywhere.

This reverses an earlier decision

Commit 9360dddd replaced a snackbar with this dialog precisely because "a snackbar auto-dismisses, so the one warning a participant gets could go unseen".

That reasoning held when there was nothing else on screen carrying the warning. There is now: the rail chip. What went away with the snackbar was the interruption, not the information.

The residual risk is real and unchanged: someone presenting full screen, or looking away for twelve seconds, gets no second prompt. If that turns out to matter, the honest fix is a second notice in the last minute, not a modal.

Left over from the dialog

The OK button on the left artboard is drawn as the code renders it in dark mode. The confirm dialog sets its label to --ov-meet-text-on-primary, which is only ever defined in the light emitter, so it stays #ffffff while the Material filled button turns pale cyan.

This flow no longer uses that dialog, but every other confirm dialog in the app still does.
